newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT DISCUSSES BUDGET BEFORE CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT DISCUSSES BUDGET BEFORE CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: The Czech government will meet on Monday to try to resolve differences on the 1997 state budget ahead of a crucial parliamentary confidence vote on Tuesday.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news briefing the centre-right coalition agreed the agenda early on Monday.
"We discussed the willingness of our three political parties to talk about cutting state expenditure at a session of the government this afternoon," he said.

Klaus said that although there were differences between the parties, as Josef Lux's Christain Democrats (KDU-CSL) and Michal Zantovsky's Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) insist on a balanced 1997 budget, they were not insurmountable.
"I would say that the essence of our differences do not concern millions or in different areas, but more on the conceptual level," he said.

The Prime Minister added that the coalition leaders agreed on the need to resolve the budget dispute, that spending cuts must be evenly spread out among government departments, and that some increases in social support must be forthcoming to soften the blow to vulnerable sections of society.
Details would be forthcoming later in the day, Klaus said.
The government pledged at the end of May to further slash public spending after promising to cut 25.5 billion crowns as part of programme of economic revival announced in mid-April.
It is not yet clear how substantial the total level of the budget cuts will be.
